task.caption_snippet: Synthetic single-panel LSV benchmark chart, variant 08. Scenario: semi-log polarization representation.
task.special_notes: Benchmark task seeded as a single-panel linear sweep voltammetry / polarization curve benchmark panel; route it through anchoring and curve extraction even if it is not LSV. Inspect the image only and do not use external source files.

x.visible_pattern: Evenly spaced numeric ticks from 0.1 to 0.6 along the horizontal axis.
x.justification: Axis-fit validation chose a linear model for x with normalized RMSE about 0.0003, far better than the log10 alternative.

y.visible_pattern: Major vertical ticks are labeled by decades (10^-1, 10^0, 10^1, 10^2) with near-equal spacing in pixel space.
y.justification: Axis-fit validation chose a log10 model for y with normalized RMSE about 0.0003, far better than the linear alternative.

unresolved_ambiguities: No explicit panel letter is printed in the image; the record was anchored as the sole panel in this single-panel figure.

response.overlap_recovery_reason: The three legend-mapped curves are fully separable across the main plot with no meaningful occlusion.

response.interpretation_notes: Main plot contains three monotonic semilog-y traces matched to legend entries A, B, and C. Sampling follows only the plot-region strokes and excludes axis/frame/legend ink.

advisories.note: For marker-bearing curves, strong near-border fractions can indicate marker-rim or frame-lock tracing even when color overlap is high. Hollow-marker centerline traces use relaxed stroke-overlap thresholds only when marker-center alignment is also good.

panel_acceptance.pass: all curves pass and no pairwise review flags
panel_acceptance.warn: no curve fails, but at least one curve warns or at least one pair is overlap-flagged
panel_acceptance.fail: at least one curve fails stroke agreement or extent coverage
